paper.title: Algorithm 911: Multiple-precision exponential integral and related functions (with the FM/ZM multiple-precision package, sample driver)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 37(4), article 46 (TOMS 911, Dec 2010)
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article itself was not read (paywalled), so the claim rests on the shipped sample driver output Fortran95/Drivers/SampleFM.out.

code.note: Fortran 95. Extract the zip; sources Fortran95/Src/FM.f95, FMZM90.f95, fmsave.f95 and the sample driver Fortran95/Drivers/SampleFM.f95 (PROGRAM SAMPLE, writes SampleFM.out). Compile with gfortran -O3 as the manual describes (Doc/FM_User_Manual.txt section on SampleFM). Do not run inside the site directory; use a fresh directory.

claim.location: The shipped sample driver output Fortran95/Drivers/SampleFM.out, sample 2 ("Find the root above to 500 decimal places"). Its printed value is the Newton root of f(x)=x**5-3x**4+x**3-4x**2+x-6 from sample 1. The first 80 significant digits are registered. The paper location was not read; no paper table or page is cited.
claim.metric: Real root of f(x)=x**5-3x**4+x**3-4x**2+x-6 = 0 computed by Newton iteration in the FM package at 500-digit precision (CALL FM_SET(500) in the sample), compared with the printed digits.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read; the value is taken from the shipped driver output.

values.name: real root of x**5-3x**4+x**3-4x**2+x-6 (SampleFM.out sample 2, 500-digit value rounded to double; the first 16 significant digits are 3.120656215326726)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The gate needs a numeric value, so the claim is the printed 500-digit root rounded to double precision, 3.1206562153267265 (true digits 3.12065621532672650047...; rounding error 4.7e-18). Tolerance 1e-15 absorbs double-precision rounding of a correctly computed root. A run that computes the root at double precision still passes; the full 500-digit agreement is checked by the rerun only as a note, not by this gate. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 15 minutes: compile of FM.f95 (about 1.8 MB) and FMZM90.f95 with gfortran -O3, then one short run.
cost.data_size: None; the sample driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic multiple-precision arithmetic package whose shipped sample prints a 500-digit root, so the claim tests the high-precision Newton arithmetic at digits far beyond double precision.
